name: MagicX Zero 28
identify: helperFunctions.sh: /usr/magicx present (the oakMOSS marker); /usr/magicx/device selects the model, falls back to Zero28 when absent/unrecognized

pad.note: simplepad, a UART MCU pad; d-pad/MENU/volume are plain keys, A/B/X/Y and the triggers too, the sticks are joystick axes (js0 on the same node). The capture is the stock MagicX image (2026-09-21), before oakMOSS: node name is resolved by MagicXCommon.sh's oakmoss_resolve_event_paths (match on kernel device name 'magicx-input'), unchanged by the base swap, but a fallback event number could differ

L3.note: the left stick's click; measured GPIO edge THUMB_L in the 2026-09-21 stock-image capture

R3.note: the right stick's click; measured GPIO edge THUMB_R in the 2026-09-21 stock-image capture

MENU.note: KEY_BACK; on an older image with MagicX's second codes (OAKMOSS_PAD_RIDERS=1) the same press also sends 353 on A, not on MENU itself

absent.HOME: cfg B_HOME=DOESNT_EXIST (unconditional, unlike the XU20's conditional Home); the 2026-09-21 stock-image capture logged one BTN_G GPIO edge (interrupt 202) on the same pin family as the XU20's Home button, but no cfg path ever reads it on this board - needs a hardware check for a real cap/button over it
absent.FN_SWITCH: no switch; device_get_switch_position is the oakMOSS no-op stub on MagicX boards (oakmoss_a133p.sh: the TrimUI PH19 pin is L1 here)
absent.FN_LEFT: no Fn key separate from L3/R3; none declared
absent.FN_RIGHT: no Fn key separate from L3/R3; none declared
absent.LID: no lid; not a clamshell, no hall node in this board's tree

notes: The 2026-09-21 discovery capture is the stock MagicX image, before oakMOSS (task framing): node names (magicx-input, axp2202-pek) are expected to carry over because MagicXCommon.sh resolves them by the same kernel device name, but this has not been re-measured on an oakMOSS build.
A hardware run should press L3/R3 (stick clicks) and try the G-button pin (if a tester can find it) to settle the HOME question, and should confirm MENU=158 with no rider on a current oakMOSS image.
